text: {"lessons":["Selling 100 shares each of A, B and E after steep losses, then buying them back the next period, shows I should avoid treating a loss alone as a reason to sell and reassess the investment case before reversing a trade.","Buying D while selling other holdings changed my portfolio’s exposure; I should check concentration and the role of each holding before reallocating money.","My account fell over these periods despite a brief rebound, so I should judge progress over a longer horizon and against a clear plan rather than focusing on month-to-month moves."]}
